expectations.text: Does NOT simply recommend a paired t-test and interpret the mean difference as evidence of improved psychological safety
expectations.evidence: The response opens 'not yet — and the reason isn't statistical power, it's measurement' and explicitly defers any paired t-test interpretation until after invariance testing. It states 'Run the invariance sequence before you touch a paired t-test.'

expectations.text: Raises longitudinal measurement invariance as a prerequisite for interpreting the pre-post score difference
expectations.evidence: The response dedicates a full section 'What you need to test: longitudinal measurement invariance' and frames it explicitly as a prerequisite: 'Before you interpret that M = 3.9 → 4.4 shift as evidence of improved psychological safety, you need to establish longitudinal measurement invariance.'

expectations.text: Explains that training programs can change how respondents interpret and use scale items (response shift, referent recalibration)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly names 'response shift, referent recalibration, reconceptualization' and explains at length how a mindfulness program can change 'how employees interpret survey items and calibrate their responses.' Also cites the Golembiewski et al. (1976) alpha/beta/gamma change taxonomy.

expectations.text: States that without invariance testing, a mean shift could reflect a real construct change OR a change in how respondents use the scale
expectations.evidence: The response states: 'Your observed mean difference (Δ = 0.5) then conflates real construct change with scale recalibration, and you can't tell which it is — or in what proportion — without testing.' Repeated in the bottom line: 'you don't know whether you're seeing a real construct change, a recalibration of how employees use the scale, or some mixture of the two.'

expectations.text: Names or implies the configural/metric/scalar invariance sequence as what would need to be tested
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly names and defines all three levels: 'Configural invariance,' 'Metric (weak) invariance,' and 'Scalar (strong) invariance,' and provides working R code implementing the full configural → metric → scalar sequence with lavaan.

expectations.text: Does not conflate 'statistically significant pre-post difference' with 'training improved psychological safety' without the measurement caveat
expectations.evidence: Significance is addressed only conditionally ('If invariance holds at scalar level, then you're in good shape to compare latent means. At that point, you can run the latent mean comparison... and a statistically significant difference... is meaningful'). The caveat is integral throughout, not appended as an afterthought.
